title: At the konbini
summary: The convenience store runs on a script. Learn the clerk's three questions, how to ask for what you want, and how to pay.
canDo: I can understand and answer the clerk's usual questions.
I can ask whether a shop has something and order a number of items.
I can ask to pay by card and close the exchange politely.
grammar: はい、お願いします・いいえ、大丈夫です

items.note: No reply needed. A nod is fine.
The gentle way to turn something down.
Swap in anything you are looking for.

items.back: Confirms what was just said: "…, right?"

items.front: カード{は|wa}{使|つか}えますか

items.back: I don't have one. / There isn't any.

items.front: ありがとうございました
items.back: Thank you (for what was just done).
items.note: The past form closes an exchange.

lessons.title: The clerk's questions
lessons.canDo: I can understand what the clerk is offering and say yes or no politely.

intro.scene: A convenience store near the hotel. Leo puts a boxed meal on the counter.

lines.text: {袋|ふくろ}{は|wa}ご{利用|りよう}ですか。
いいえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
お{弁当|べんとう}{は|wa}{温|あたた}めますか。
lines.meaning: Shall I heat up the meal?

lines.text: はい、お{願|ねが}いします。
お{箸|はし}{は|wa}ご{利用|りよう}ですか。

notes.title: Catch the noun
notes.body: Clerks speak very politely: ご{利用|りよう}ですか means "will you be using…?". You do not need to produce it. Listen for the first word: {袋|ふくろ} bag, お{箸|はし} chopsticks, レシート receipt.

notes.title: Two answers cover everything
notes.body: はい、お{願|ねが}いします for yes. いいえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です for no. {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ} means "all right", so you are saying "I'm fine without it".

notes.title: {温|あたた}めますか
notes.body: A verb you know the shape of: 〜ますか. "Shall I heat it?" Answer the same two ways.

exercises.prompt: Listen. What is the clerk offering?
exercises.text: {袋|ふくろ}{は|wa}ご{利用|りよう}ですか。

exercises.prompt: You don't need a bag. The natural answer is:
options: いいえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
いいえ、{袋|ふくろ}じゃありません。
exercises.explain: ちがいます means "that is incorrect". To decline an offer, use {大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です.

exercises.prompt: Answer: "Yes, please."
exercises.context: お{弁当|べんとう}{は|wa}{温|あたた}めますか。
exercises.answer: はい、お{願|ねが}いします

exercises.prompt: The clerk says いらっしゃいませ as you walk in. What should you do?
options: Say いらっしゃいませ back
exercises.explain: It is a greeting from staff to customers, not something customers say.

exercises.prompt: Type in Japanese: "No, I'm fine."
exercises.answer: いいえ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。

exercises.meaning: I don't need the receipt, thanks.

lessons.title: Do you have…? Two of these, please
lessons.canDo: I can ask if a shop has something and order one, two or three of it.

intro.scene: Back at the same store the next morning, at the hot-food counter.

lines.text: すみません、コーヒー{は|wa}ありますか。
lines.meaning: Excuse me, do you have coffee?

lines.text: じゃあ、コーヒーを{一|ひと}つと、{肉|にく}まんを{二|ふた}つください。
lines.meaning: Then one coffee and two meat buns, please.

lines.text: コーヒーを{一|ひと}つ、{肉|にく}まんを{二|ふた}つですね。
lines.meaning: One coffee and two meat buns, right?

lines.text: {全部|ぜんぶ}で{五百円|ごひゃくえん}です。

notes.title: 〜{は|wa}ありますか
notes.body: "Do you have…?" Name the thing and add {は|wa}ありますか. The answers are あります (we do) and ありません (we don't).

notes.title: Counting things: 〜つ
notes.body: {一|ひと}つ, {二|ふた}つ, {三|みっ}つ, {四|よっ}つ, {五|いつ}つ. This all-purpose counter works for almost anything you can order.

notes.title: Where the number goes
notes.body: Thing + を + number + ください: コーヒーを{二|ふた}つください. The number comes after を and takes no particle of its own.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap.
Build: "Two coffees, please."
exercises.answer: コーヒーを{二|ふた}つください

exercises.prompt: Which order is right?
options: おにぎりを{三|みっ}つください。
{三|みっ}つをおにぎりください。
おにぎりの{三|みっ}つをください。
exercises.explain: Thing, を, number, ください.

exercises.prompt: Listen. What is the clerk confirming?
exercises.text: {肉|にく}まんを{二|ふた}つですね。

exercises.prompt: How do you say "one (thing)"?
exercises.explain: The 〜つ counter has its own readings: ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ.

exercises.prompt: Type in Japanese: "Three, please."
alt: {三|みっ}つお{願|ねが}いします。

exercises.prompt: Reply: "Yes. Water too, please."
exercises.context: コーヒーを{一|ひと}つですね。
exercises.answer: はい。{水|みず}もください
exercises.explain: も takes the place of を, just as it replaces は.

exercises.prompt: Match the counter with the number.

meme.bottom: Also Japanese: ひとつ, ふたつ, みっつ. Surprise!

lessons.title: Paying and leaving
lessons.canDo: I can answer the point-card question, ask to pay by card, and say thank you as I leave.

intro.scene: At the till. There is a queue, so everything goes quickly.

lines.text: ポイントカード{は|wa}お{持|も}ちですか。
lines.meaning: Do you have a point card?

lines.text: {全部|ぜんぶ}で{八百円|はっぴゃくえん}です。
カード{は|wa}{使|つか}えますか。
はい、{使|つか}えます。こちらにタッチしてください。
lines.meaning: Yes, you can. Please tap here.

lines.text: ありがとうございました。

notes.title: お{持|も}ちですか
notes.body: Another polite clerk phrase: "do you have … with you?". Again, catch the noun: ポイントカード. If you have none: いいえ、ありません.

notes.title: カード{は|wa}{使|つか}えますか
notes.body: Learn it whole for now: "can I use a card?". Most konbini take cards and transport IC cards, but small restaurants and shrines are often cash only.

notes.title: ありがとうございました
notes.body: The past form of ありがとうございます. Staff say it when the exchange is finished, and you can say it back as you leave.

exercises.prompt: Listen. What is the clerk asking?

options: Do you have a point card?

options: はい、お{願|ねが}いします。

exercises.prompt: The clerk says こちらにタッチしてください. What do you do?
options: Tap your card on the reader
exercises.explain: こちら = here (polite). タッチ = tap.

exercises.prompt: You have paid and are leaving. Type in Japanese: "Thank you."
exercises.answer: ありがとうございました。
alt: ありがとうございます。
どうもありがとうございました。

exercises.prompt: Listen. What is the total?
